steps.text: Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add carrots, onion, and garlic; cook and stir until tender, about 10 minutes. Add ground beef; cook, stirring and breaking up meat, until browned, 5 to 7 minutes. Drain off excess fat from the skillet.
Stir in 1 cup milk; bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to medium-low and cook until milk is absorbed, about 15 minutes.

Transfer beef mixture to a slow cooker and set to High. Stir in crushed tomatoes, tomato paste, basil, oregano, salt, pepper, and red pepper flakes. Cover and cook on High for 2 hours. Stir in remaining ½ cup milk and Parmesan; cook for 2 more hours.

raw_recipe.headline: Slow Cooker Bolognese
raw_recipe.description: Slow cooker Bolognese made with ground beef, milk, tomatoes, and Parmesan simmers in a crockpot to make a hearty and rich, comforting pasta sauce.
raw_recipe.name: Slow Cooker Bolognese

review.reviewBody: Hi - this is my recipe and I just wanted to note that I have switched from using 1 lb ground beef to 1 lb "meatloaf mix" (a ground beef/pork blend) and it really enhances the flavor of the sauce. Enjoy! :)

This was worth the extra trouble! I am temporarily disabled and can't stand up very long but the recipe looked so good that I had to ty it. I used my small chopper to chop up the carrots and added 1/2 a cup of chopped celery. I was a bit leery of using milk with ground beef but the sauce was so rich and had a wonderful texture that I'll be making this again. Since I live alone, I'll freeze some of it. Thank you for sharing this great recipe.

Wow this was great. I cooked the carrots, garlic and onions first along with the seasoning to toast it a bit. I put that into the crock pot. Next I browned the meat and cooked it with milk. Put that into the crock. I sautéed a bunch of sliced white and crimini mushrooms along with the tomato paste then dumped them in. I used some canned san Marzano tomatoes and a can of tomato puree. I let it cook for a few extra hours though and the flavor was fantastic. Will definitely make this again.

This is fabulous, but I made just a few changes: I added so much more garlic (2 heads); I ended up adding 2 whole red peppers, also; I used fresh basil towards the end of the cooking time; I ended up cutting short the cooking time because it seemed to cook much more quickly. I loved the addition of the milk (I used half and half) for a creamier sauce. Next time, I think I'll add some ground sausage for even more flavour.

As per other suggestions, I browned meat first, drained fat, removed from pan. Then sautéed carrots, celery, onion and garlic using an herb infused olive oil. Tossed meat back into pan & followed instructions from there. I will definitely make this again. It was a giant hit. Thanks for the recipe

Omitted the carrots, doubled the onion and basil, extended cooking time by an hour but last hour was placed on low. In the last hour, I added a mixture of 1/2 c Gouda, 1/2 cheddar in last hour, and a half a cup of chicken stock.

My family consumed EVERYTHING. Feedback was phenomenal.

I think this is quite good but I was afraid to add the milk. I put part in at the end but that affected the taste. Be sure to add the milk early on. Also next time I will do the oven or stove top. Also be more careful about browning the meat at the beginning. I did use half pork and half beef. I also goofed and added extra tomato, so it turned out reddish. I’ll be making again and sticking closer to the recipe. It’s a comfort food.
This is an excellent bolognese. The only thing I changed is I added a splash of bold red wine at the end. And I also added a small parmesan rind. I served it on tagliatelle instead of rigatoni.

This sauce is good to eat and easy to make. I agree with the member who said you should drain the grease first, then add the veggies and simmer, otherwise you lose some depth of flavor. We also used a combo of beef and pork. Speaking of depth of flavor, I used hunts tomato sauce and paste, the sauce is too tangy, but I am almost certain it is due to the paste or tomatoes. If anyone has any suggestions for another brand with better flavor, let me know! I also added more spices and cheese than the recipe calls for, using both asiago and parmesean. I usually like my food a little heavy on the spice. It also helped with the tang. Think i may use heavy cream in place of milk next time. Thank you, OP. My family really enjoyed their meal tonight!

This sauce is thick and has a deep rich flavor. To save time and get the sauce simmering in the crock pot more quickly, I cooked the carrots and onions in the oil in one pan while browning the meat then simmering it with the milk in a second pan.

Best sauce I have ever made. I did use meatloaf mix, And 3 garlic cloves. Followed directions except I did add rest of the milk and the cheese as soon as I put everything in the crock pot. I chopped carrots, onion, garlic in a food processor so the pieces were so small any picky eaters could not tell (by the looks) that they were in there.

Absolutely, Positively the best Bolognese I have ever made. I tweak most recipes to suit our taste. Here are the things I did differently with this one: I added a couple stalks of chopped celery (in with the carrots, onions, garlic). I used half & half instead of whole milk. I added a splash of wine , about 1/4 cup, (I will add 1/2 cup next time). Incredibly Delicious! Thank you so much!! I wish my 100% pure Italian father & grandmother were still here so I could have them over for it.

Loved the recipe, think it was the best slow cooker bolognaise sauce I ever found! I substituted a whole yellow sweet pepper for the carrot, and added a beef bouillon cube in the slow cooker for added flavour. I was hesitant about the milk, however at the end I think it provides a nice rich body to the sauce! Overall, an excellent recipe!

Is it authentic bolognese? No. But does it hit the spot? Yes! Really liked this one, especially with the rigatoni. I added in a little red wine at the end for some pazzazz and it hit the spot. I made this for two and had the perfect amount for leftovers, which I’ll freeze and use on a rainy (cold!) day.

Excellent! I used half & half to evaporate into the ground meat. Really adds richness and makes a difference! Just put all in the slow cooker. Can't wait for the last two hours to add more half & half and parm. Great recipe!
Love this bolognese sauce. Definitely will make again.
I have made this recipe several times. It's my favorite bolognese. Very easy to make and tastes great! Love serving it over pappardelle.
Great and easy to follow recipe. It was thick and rich and had a very smooth taste. One of the best I've had!
Just wonderful. Rich, decadent and unctuous! Worth the time and effort.
Needs celery?
